subject: Crest vs baseline: streaming concurrency & dwell sizing (post-call)
messages:
From: Hannah Li <hannah.li@fleetops.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@fleetops.io>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: throughput profile we walked through today

Thanks for the time earlier — quick recap from our side and a couple clarifications so you can size the pilot. Good call.

Summary of observable traffic (attached: fleetops-traffic-snapshot-20260514.csv):
- Baseline: ~9 QPS (desktop web API), median request payload ~320 tokens (text + metadata).
- Crest/peak events: short bursts when our routing engine triggers batch enrichments — observed up to 260 QPS for ~40-90s windows (peaks often come as a series of crests across the hour).
- Streaming sessions: chat-like flows for support assistants. Concurrent streams ~160 active at peak; each stream averages 18 tokens/sec once established, total session duration variable (30s–6m).
- Typical synchronous (non-stream) requests during peaks average 420 tokens.
- KV cache: ~35% hit rate currently (we expect to improve).

Questions we need help with:
1) What P95 latency can Redwood hit for streaming sessions with 160 concurrent streams and our peak QPS pattern? We want practical SLO targets to propose internally.
2) For pilot sizing, can you map crest durations vs reserve capacity recommendations? We want a small Reserved pool for baseline + a burst plan.
3) Any guidance on concurrent-open-stream limits per model and whether continued prefix-KV caching changes sizing?

Next actions we expect: sample sizing proposal + recommended P95 latency SLOs and a candidate pilot window (we're targeting early June).

Thanks — Hannah
FleetOps

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Li <hannah.li@fleetops.io>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@fleetops.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 16:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput profile we walked through today

Hannah — thanks for the concise snapshot and the CSV. Quick read-through and a high-level mapping below. I attached a one-pager forecast (crest-dwell-forecast.xlsx) you can use for your procurement team.

High-level mapping (candidate SLOs we typically propose for this shape):
- Streaming: target P95 end-to-end frame latency <= 250ms for established streams when concurrent streams <= 200 and per-frame tokens <= 32.
- Non-stream gen (sync): P95 token-latency target <= 400ms for requests up to 500 tokens; for requests >500 tokens we recommend a relaxed P95 (<= 750ms) or a batch/async pattern.

Sizing heuristics from your snapshot: (rough conversions)
- Baseline token throughput: 9 QPS * 320 tokens ~= 2.9k tokens/sec sustained.
- Peak crest: 260 QPS * 420 tokens ~= 109k tokens/sec during crest windows (40–90s).
- Concurrent streaming tokens: 160 streams * 18 tok/s ~= 2.9k tokens/sec (streams add pressure to concurrency rather than peak QPS).

Pilot recommendation:
- Reserved pool: cover baseline + 20% headroom (recommend equivalent of 12 QPS steady).
- Burst plan: autoscale policy with two-tier capacity — short-lived burst nodes optimized for crest durations up to 120s and fallback to a warm pool if crest extends beyond that.
- KV cache assumption: with a 35% hit rate, plan for ~65% cache-miss load on peak; if you improve hit to 60% we can reduce reserve footprint by ~15%.

Questions I still have (can you confirm):
- Are the crest windows typically contiguous (one 40–90s window) or a rapid series of smaller crests over the hour?
- For streaming: how many concurrent streams are long-lived (>3 minutes) vs short (<1 minute)?

I'll loop in Eng (Marissa, Jonas) to validate the SLOs and give an initial slot/pool proposal. Proposed follow-up: 30-min sizing review with your infra lead next week.

Thanks — Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Hannah Li <hannah.li@fleetops.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput profile we walked through today

Adding a quick engineering lens — thanks for the data Hannah. A few implementation notes that affect sizing and SLO realism:

1) Streaming concurrency effects
- Open streaming sessions consume a slot for the KV cache and maintain a small per-stream state; at 160 concurrent streams the main impact is memory and context-switch overhead rather than per-token compute. We can hit the 250ms P95 target if the per-frame token payload is small (<=32) and streams reuse a warm worker set. If many streams are long-lived with periodic bursts, we recommend a dedicated streaming pool to avoid head-of-line latency on sync requests.

2) Crest modeling and autoscale
- For crest windows 40–90s we recommend an aggressive short-burst autoscaler (scale up within 20s) backed by a warm pool sized for typical crest amplitude (we'd size for ~50% of observed crest as a warm pool and autoscale the rest). For your 260 QPS crest this implies: warm pool capacity ~= 130 QPS equivalent; ephemeral burst nodes to cover the remaining delta.

3) Quantization and batch tradeoffs
- If you can allow 4-bit quantized models in the pilot we can increase effective throughput per GPU ~1.8x which materially reduces reserve needs. For large sync requests (>400 tokens) batching helps but at the cost of tail latency; recommend batching only for background enrichments.

Action items / owners:
- Jonas: draft a pilot pool config (warm pool size, burst window, autoscale thresholds) and estimate expected P95 under current cache-hit assumptions.
- Neha: prepare a short runbook for stream pool failover and fallback to non-stream variant if latency slips.
- Rishi: confirm pilot window with FleetOps and send proposed slot numbers after Jonas' draft.

I'll aim to have Jonas' draft by EOD Tue (May 19).

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@fleetops.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput profile we walked through today

Appreciate the rapid answers and the proposed approach. Quick confirm from our side:
- Crest patterns are usually clustered (series of 30–90s crests over a 20–40 minute window) not a single spike.
- Concurrent streams: about 40% are long-lived (>3m), rest are short interactions.

FleetOps is happy to target early June for a 2-week pilot. We approve running quantized models for the pilot if it simplifies sizing and reduces cost.

Next steps we want on calendar:
1) 30-min pilot sizing sync (include Jonas + Neha) — please propose slots; Rishi to coordinate.
2) Pilot kickoff doc + expected acceptance criteria (P95 targets for streaming and sync, error budget window).

Thanks — Tom
